ref.locator: Input 1: DOC 56 1470/001, Tabel 1 'Aangepaste programma's', PDF p. 795-805, section 17, divisions 17-40 (CG + SAT), 17-41 (DGA), 17-42 (DGJ), 17-43 (DGR) and 17-44 (common personnel costs), all basic allocations with economic code 11 except B.A. 17 44 12 11.00.03 (end-of-career scheme NAVAP); adjusted 2026 credits, x 1 000 EUR (commitment = liquidation for all of them). Input 2: DOC 56 1279/003 (Court of Audit), PDF p. 64 (printed p. 62), point 5.4 'Sectie 17 - Federale politie en geïntegreerde werking'.
ref.quote: Input 1 (main rows): '40 11 11.00.03 ... 183.470'; '41 11 11.00.03 ... 344.258'; '42 11 11.00.03 ... 357.728'; '43 11 11.00.03 ... 106.507'; excluded: 'Financiering eindeloopbaanregime van de federale politie 44 12 11.00.03 15.627'. Input 2: 'Het Rekenhof wijst er echter op dat het aantal beschikbare personeelsleden eind 2025 (13.980 VTE) nauwelijks hoger is dan het aantal personeelsleden in 2021 (13.962 VTE).'
ref.note: Checked by a second agent: Re-added all allocations myself: there are 29 economic-code-11 allocations in divisions 40-44 (4 each in 40, 41, 42 and 43, and 13 in 44). Each is a pay or personnel allocation (salaries, inconvenience allowances, social security, commuting refunds, meal vouchers, secondments, police catering staff, traffic-safety inconvenience allowances). None is double counted and none of code 11 is missing; the sum 1,204,032 thousand EUR is correct, as is 1,204,032,000 / 13,980 = 86,125. Correction: B.A. 17 44 12 11.00.03 'Financiering eindeloopbaanregime van de federale politie' (15,627) pays the end-of-career scheme NAVAP (non-activity before retirement; the Court of Audit on PDF p. 64-65 calls it 'de eindeloopbaanregeling voor de politie (NAVAP, deel Federale Politie voor 15,6 miljoen euro)'). These people are not part of the 13,980 'available' FTE, so I removed it from the numerator: 1,204,032 - 15,627 = 1,188,405 thousand EUR; 1,188,405,000 / 13,980 = 85,007.51, rounded 85,008 EUR. All allocations are in section 17 and the federal police line is section 17 minus the zone grants, so they are inside the line. Remaining caveats: (1) The headcount is the end-2025 actual, and the 2026 credits are sized for the 14,280 FTE target (dividing by that gives 83,222), so the figure may be up to about 2% high. (2) Secondment allocations 44 13/14/15 (29.1 million) are kept, but it is unclear whether those staff are in the 'available' count. (3) Excluded: aspirants (17-80, 61.6 million), staff in 17-80 (GCC/seconded-in 2.2 million, traffic-safety common purchases 11.5 million), the SSGPI secretariat (17-81), flat-rate expense allowances (economic code 12.11.99) and payments for seconded-in staff (12.21.x). (4) Police pensions are not included (they are paid from the civil-service-pensions line). The label says it is an average over officers and civilian staff together, not the cost of one inspector. Researcher's working: Sum of all economic-code-11 allocations (adjusted 2026 credits, x 1 000 EUR): division 40: 183,470 + 2,469 + 22,235 + 108 = 208,282; division 41: 344,258 + 1,739 + 61,530 + 189 = 407,716; division 42: 357,728 + 2,072 + 29,347 + 26 = 389,173; division 43: 106,507 + 16,095 + 2,952 + 245 = 125,799; division 44: 1,806 + 41 + 7,026 + 14,591 + 15,627 + 10,976 + 1,159 + 16,971 + 1,876 + 250 + 2,726 + 2 + 11 = 73,062. Total 1,204,032 thousand EUR. 1,204,032,000 / 13,980 FTE (end 2025) = 86,125.32 EUR, rounded to 86,125 EUR. Average over all federal police staff (operational officers and civilian CALog staff), not specifically a starting inspector; a beginning inspector costs less and a senior officer more. Excludes police trainees (division 17-80), the integrated-police secretariat (17-81), operating and investment costs, and police pensions (civil-service-pensions line). Headcount (end 2025) and credits (2026) are from different dates; the 2026 staffing target is 14,280 FTE. The sum covers about 30 budget allocations, so a reviewer should re-add them from pages 795-805. A starting inspector's salary scale (jobpol.be) and police.be staffing figures could not be checked: both sites returned HTTP 403.

ref.quote: Op het personeelsvlak hebben de voornaamste (recurrente) projecten betrekking op het rekruteren, selecteren, uitrusten, opleiden en verlonen van de aspiranten.
ref.note: Excludes the federal grants to local police zones (separate line). Recruitment and basic training of aspirants is organised federally for the integrated police (federal and local). Most of the line is statutory pay of federal police staff, with pay scales set by regulation. corrected: locator only (DG judicial police starts p. 48; organised drug trafficking named at p. 54). Quote confirmed verbatim at DOC 56 1281/009 p. 102; road, railway and aviation police at p. 29; police schools p. 120. Phrases confirmed.
